title: Trump signed Title IX sports executive order on February 5, 2025
description_short: Trump signed Title IX sports executive order on February 5, 2025
description_medium: On February 5, 2025, Trump signed “Keeping Men Out of Women’s Sports,” directing federal agencies to apply the administration’s interpretation of Title IX to schools that permit transgender girls and women to compete in female sports categories and to review relevant grants. The order’s issuance does not establish that every school immediately changed its policy or lost federal funding.
description_long_previous: President Donald Trump signed the executive order “Keeping Men Out of Women’s Sports” on February 5, 2025—not January 20. It directs federal agencies to apply the administration’s interpretation of Title IX to schools that allow transgender girls and women to compete in female sports categories and to consider grant and funding consequences. This is a description of the order’s directives, not evidence that every federally funded school immediately adopted a ban or that any particular school lost funding. The cited order does not document the alleged post-order surge in bullying or establish health outcomes for transgender students. Those claims require separate, specific evidence and are excluded from this correction.
description_long: President Donald Trump signed the executive order “Keeping Men Out of Women’s Sports” on February 5, 2025. The order sets federal policy opposing male participation in women’s sports and directs agencies to apply the administration’s interpretation of Title IX. It instructs the education secretary, coordinating with the attorney general, to continue complying with the court vacatur of the 2024 Title IX rule, take action to ensure that rule has no effect, protect all-female athletic opportunities and locker rooms, align regulations and guidance with the order’s interpretation, and prioritize enforcement against educational institutions that require female students to compete in women’s sports against males or appear unclothed before males. A separate provision directs federal agencies to review grants to educational programs and, where appropriate, rescind funding from programs that fail to comply with the order’s policy. The order also directs the White House domestic policy assistant to convene athletic organizations, affected female athletes, and state attorneys general within 60 days. These are stated directives; the order does not establish implementation at every school, any particular grant termination, a post-order bullying increase, or student-health outcomes.

The order alone does not establish immediate blanket implementation at every federally funded school or any specific funding loss.
